newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Nigeria sends more troops, hardware to Freetown.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria sends more troops, hardware to Freetown.

text.p: Nigeria flew more troops and military hardware into Sierra Leone on Friday, ahead of an expected regional intervention to restore the civilian president ousted in a coup last weekend, military sources in the Liberian capital said.
Ghana said it was consulting with Nigeria and Guinea on the situation in Freetown, from where hundreds of foreigners have been evacuated.

West African leaders have agreed to support a Nigerian-led intervention to restore ousted president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah. Nigeria leads the ECOMOG regional intervention sent to Liberia in 1990, which also has some troops in Sierra Leone.
Military sources in Monrovia said two transport planes had flown Nigerian armoured personnel carriers and jeeps into Freetown to join hundreds of men already on the ground.
Ghana's army prepared troop transport planes, officially to evacuate Ghanaian nationals living in Sierra Leone.
One report said Guinea had flown in 500 men on Thursday night but this could not immediately be confirmed.

"We cannot tell you now when we will be leaving for Sierra Leone, with how many men and with how many planes. We are still working on getting the personnel and other arrangements," Ghana Armed Forces spokesman Major John Simmons told Reuters.
Simmons declined to say whether the Ghanaian troops would support a military intervention by Nigeria.
Ghana's President Jerry Rawlings formed an emergency committee, made up mainly of army generals, to monitor the situtation in Sierra Leone on an hourly basis, state media said.

"Ghana is studying the situation in Sierra Leone seriously, in collaboration with Nigeria and Guinea, in order to act swiftly if the situation deteriorates," Kofi Totobi Quakyi, acting information minister, told reporters on Wednesday.
On Tuesday, Ghana's High Commission in Freetown was attacked by armed gangs, who unsuccessfully tried to steal embassy cars.
Ghana has 30 men and four officers stationed at Lungi Airport in connection with ECOMOG operations in neighbouring Liberia.
